A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EVA research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on language generation, GLUE, VTAB-1K and Meta-World, together with ablations and convergence analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds larger-model evaluations, comparator results, initialization analyses and rank/scaling experiments.

M1.justification: The core EVA procedure remains incremental SVD of downstream activations, initialization with leading right-singular vectors, explained-variance rank redistribution, zero initialization of B and LoRA fine-tuning. Algorithm 2 elaborates the existing incremental computation; the new minor-component and scaling experiments test variants rather than replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same commonsense tasks, MetaMathQA with GSM8K/MATH evaluation, Code-Feedback with coding benchmarks, GLUE, VTAB-1K and Meta-World MT40/CW10. The added 27B and 70B language models expand model configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds LoRA-GA to commonsense and mathematical reasoning comparisons and initialization timing measurements (Tables 9–10 and 25). Table 11 also includes MiLoRA at rank 16, while Table 12 compares LoRA and EVA under LoRA+ and rsLoRA adaptations. These substantially expand the evaluated alternatives, particularly direct data-driven initialization competitors.

E3.justification: v2 adds Gemma-2-27B and Llama-3.1-70B configurations, including 4-bit base-model quantization, gradient checkpointing and ZeRO offloading for the latter. New protocols vary ranks over 8–64, scaling and learning rates, and use 20 minibatches for EVA-minor. Section 4.1 also specifies rank-dependent alpha rescaling, qualifying v1's fixed-alpha description without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds adapter-distance analyses, commonsense rank and scaling controls, major-versus-minor component comparisons, parameter-count analyses and comparative initialization timings (Tables 7–8, 11–14 and 25), plus additional loss curves. v1's gradient-norm analysis disappears from Figure 2. The original VTAB ablations remain in Appendix I and Table 26.

E5.justification: The existing three- or five-seed benchmark reporting and standard-deviation/standard-error conventions are retained. v2 Table 25 newly states that training time is averaged across two runs. This is limited additional repeated-run information; expanded standard-deviation tables and changed deviation values do not establish increased replication of existing experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including EVA commonsense averages of 93.7 for Gemma-2-27B and 94.5 for Llama-3.1-70B, alongside new comparator, ablation, parameter-count and timing results. Existing EVA commonsense entries also change, such as the Llama-3.1-8B average from 89.4 to 89.5. Changed rank/scaling reporting prevents treating this as a clean same-setting gain. Matched GLUE, vision, RL and coding tables retain their values.

T1.justification: v1's SVD and rank-allocation formulas are extended with explicit truncated-SVD approximation, adapter-gradient expressions and Eckart–Young/data-processing arguments in Section 3.2. v2 also adds incremental block-SVD derivations in Appendix F and an SVD–PCA equivalence derivation in Appendix H. This is substantial new mathematical content, independent of its correctness.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add claims that EVA provably stores the maximum downstream information and leaves training to select which information to retain. They also introduce parameter reduction and Pareto dominance as central advantages. v1 emphasized variance-based initialization, faster convergence and higher average performance without these additional optimality and efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v2 develops initialization-distance and information-preservation explanations in place of the gradient-norm explanation. It explains parameter savings through redistribution toward smaller projections, discusses model/task dependence and possible overfitting at higher ranks, recommends redistribution by default, and adds a substantive discussion of restoring base-model knowledge when B starts at zero.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed incremental-SVD pseudocode, running-moment handling, large-model quantization/offloading information and timing configurations. Appendix A replaces v1's public repository and minimal-example links with a submission-archive description, NLU/NLG directory instructions and promises of future releases and PEFT integration. This changes documented access; actual external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces PiSSA with LoRA-GA among the closest methods and acknowledges CorDA as concurrent data-driven work, revising EVA's novelty and computational-cost positioning. v2 adds mathematical and incremental-SVD foundations and removes the Hayou initialization-dynamics reference while retaining LoRA+. These are substantive changes beyond bibliographic formatting or publication-year updates.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method and discussion undergo extensive rewriting around information preservation and parameter efficiency. v2 adds an explicit contribution list, reorganizes the language-generation narrative around performance/parameter plots, and moves Section 4.7's ablations into Appendix I. Copyediting and heading-style changes accompany this substantial narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to expose component sorting and allocation. Figure 2 focuses its loss plot on early steps and replaces gradient bars with adapter distances. v2 adds parameter/performance plots, additional loss plots, Algorithm 2 and several tables. Main-text language-generation tables move to the appendix, and the original ablation table becomes Table 26.

improvement.justification: The new comparator, larger-model and rank/scaling experiments strengthen empirical assessment, and incremental-SVD documentation improves inspectability. However, the stronger information-optimality claim exceeds Appendix H's PCA argument, whose final matrix identity is also incorrect. New timing prose reports 4.8% LoRA-GA overhead whereas Table 25 reports 2.4%. Appendix A also replaces direct public code links with archive and future-release descriptions. These substantive gains and weaknesses leave the net overall quality direction uncertain.
